techniques.title: Christmas Wrapping Paper Reveal
techniques.summary: Paper covers the subject and gets torn open on camera, so the reveal itself is the announcement.
requires: something wrapped or covered in paper
the paper being torn or opened on camera
the object visible once the paper is gone

ops.opening: start on the first tear; drop the setup, taping and fiddling before it
ops.order: tear, then reveal, in the order it happened
ops.pacing: 6-12 seconds; quick through the tear, a held beat on the reveal
ops.ending: hold on the revealed object for about 1.5 seconds

techniques.title: Paid Me No Mind
techniques.summary: The same short line delivered again and again, each take stressing a different word with a bigger reaction.
requires: one person saying the same short line two or more times
the reaction growing from take to take

ops.pacing: 8-15 seconds; one beat per take, no gaps between

techniques.title: I Feel Like I Haven't Done Much This Year
techniques.summary: A deflated opening line answered by a run of clips from across the year that prove otherwise.
requires: a low-key opening line or shot about not having done much
many clips from different times or places

ops.pacing: about one second per clip, 12-20 seconds total
ops.ending: the strongest moment of the year

techniques.title: I feel like I haven't done much this year
techniques.summary: Open on the doubt, then fire off quick month-by-month clips as receipts.
requires: a low-key opening line or shot about not having done much
many clips from different times or places

ops.pacing: rapid cuts, about one second each

techniques.title: Get up, diva
techniques.summary: A setback on camera, then the shake-it-off comeback.
requires: a visible setback: a slip, a mess, a failed attempt
a recovery or comeback after it

ops.pacing: a fast cut from the fall to getting back up
ops.audio: keep the original sound of the moment

techniques.title: Outfit transition
techniques.summary: Camera stays put; one simple repeated move swaps one look for the next.
requires: a camera held in one spot
the same person in two or more looks or states
the same simple movement repeated in each

ops.pacing: cut each look at the same point of the repeated movement (match cut)
ops.ending: the strongest look, held a beat longer

techniques.title: The process
techniques.summary: Walk through the tools and steps behind something, then land on the finished result.
requires: steps of making or doing something
the finished result on camera

ops.order: steps in order, trimmed to their key frames

techniques.title: Open on the strongest line
techniques.summary: When someone is talking, the most specific or surprising sentence they say becomes the first thing heard, then the context that makes it land.
requires: someone speaking on camera
one line that is striking, specific or emotional

ops.opening: the strongest verbatim line, from its first word
ops.order: then the context that gives that line its meaning
ops.pacing: remove dead air and false starts between thoughts
ops.audio: keep speech intelligible; never cut mid-word

techniques.title: Open on the moment of change
techniques.summary: Start on the moment something starts to change and hold back the result, so the viewer stays to see it.
requires: a clear moment where something changes, opens or is revealed

ops.opening: the instant just before the change

techniques.title: Close-up to wide
techniques.summary: A tight detail first creates a small mystery that the wider shot resolves.
requires: a tight detail shot (hands, texture, label)
a wider shot of the same subject or scene

ops.pacing: two to three seconds on the detail

techniques.title: Cut the setup, open on the action
techniques.summary: The first frame is already the interesting part; setup, idle time and dead air are removed.
requires: any footage with an action or moment worth watching

ops.opening: the first frame of real action
ops.order: the action in the order it happened
ops.pacing: drop idle time and dead air
